scope_summary: Security, PHI, IG, data protection risks for LEO-AI-CORE SaMD Class B/C operating on NHS primary care data under UK GDPR. Reviewed 13 in-scope YAML risks plus 5 FMEA_GAP entries (FMEA-049/054/055/088/090 -> MR-123/127/128/150/151).

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient-identifiable data inadvertently stored in Coding terminology DB
reviews.justification: Architectural separation (physically separate Neo4j instances with independent connection strings) is an inherent-safety control aligned with UK GDPR Article 25 data-protection by design. Schema constraints + monthly automated scans + code review provide defence in depth. STRIDE-I residual probability is improbable; severity remains critical because any leak would still be an Article 33 notifiable breach. Existing controls satisfy the proportionality test for SaMD Class B.
additional_controls_required: Add CI test that asserts Coding DB schema contains no node label or property matching the Patient DB allow-list (currently relies on DI-LEO-AI-023 manual code review).
Document the monthly Coding DB PHI scan results in the DSPT evidence pack.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Keep monthly automated scan; add SIEM alert on any successful write of high-cardinality string properties to Coding DB.

reviews.title_excerpt: PHI not removed from encounter text before processing
reviews.justification: libs/deid/deid.py covers NHS number, postcode, date, phone and email regex families plus configurable org names, but acknowledged gaps exist (GAP-008: free-text patient names without title prefix, ad-hoc identifier formats, DOBs in sentence form). Mitigation YAML lists only DI-LEO-AI-023 with a single VT, which is narrower than the actual surface area. Reaches Article 25 minimum (data minimisation) but not yet fully verified to NHS DSPT 'tested against gold corpus' standard. Probability of residual leakage to displayed reviewer text/logs is judged unlikely, not remote, given current regex-only approach.
additional_controls_required: Build a labelled de-identification gold corpus (>= 500 sentences) and attach to VT-LEO-AI-014; require >= 99% recall on NHS_NUMBER, POSTCODE, EMAIL, PHONE before each release.
Add NER-based name detection (e.g., scispaCy PERSON) as a second layer behind regex (GAP-008 closure).
Wire `deidentify_with_span` (R-052 control) consistently across ALL call sites that reach reviewer UI or log sinks; today only training/evidence path is enforced.
Add CI lint rule that blocks `logger.*(encounter_text)` patterns without a `deidentify(...)` wrapper.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Monthly random sample of 500 displayed/logged sentences scanned with detect_phi(); zero detections required. Track GAP-008 closure as a DSPT KPI.

reviews.title_excerpt: Unauthorised access to patient clinical data
reviews.justification: Azure AD/Entra authentication, RBAC with org-scoped tenancy, separate DB credentials, and access audit logging are correctly layered. Aligned with UK GDPR Article 5(1)(f) integrity/confidentiality and Article 32 security of processing. Periodic access review is procedural and 'effective'. Residual probability is improbable; detectability rated 2 because privilege creep typically only surfaces at quarterly review.
additional_controls_required: Document quarterly access review evidence template and store in DSPT pack.
Add anomaly alerts (e.g., off-hours bulk patient queries) on top of access audit log.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Continue continuous Entra sign-in monitoring; add monthly review of high-cardinality patient queries per user.

reviews.title_excerpt: Prompt injection via clinical text causes LLM misbehaviour (legacy entry)
reviews.justification: R-014 is largely superseded by R-030, which captures the comprehensive injection-guard, sanitise_for_prompt, cap_llm_response, dual-model consensus and fail-safe controls. R-014 in isolation under-states the actual posture. Severity rating of 'minor' is correct because human review remains the gate for HITL flows; in autonomous flows the safe-default to UNCERTAIN bounds the harm. Recommend cross-linking R-014 -> R-030 to avoid duplicate-but-thinner mitigation listing.
additional_controls_required: Add 'see also: R-LEO-AI-030' cross-reference in R-014 YAML and consolidate mitigation list, OR retire R-014 in favour of R-030.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Use R-030 monitoring metrics (prompt_safety logger, arbitrator_third_verdict, cap_llm_response truncation).

reviews.justification: Automated CI dependency scanning + 48h critical patch SLA + quarterly DC-SOUP-001 review meet ISO 27001 A.8 and NHS DSPT vulnerability management expectations. Residual risk is medium not low because CVE residual probability is realistically 'unlikely' (not remote) given the LLM/Python/Node ecosystem velocity and the existence of unpatched-window and zero-day exposure. Conditionally acceptable provided the 48h SLA is genuinely tracked with evidence and a SBOM is published per IEC 81001-5-1.
additional_controls_required: Generate and publish a CycloneDX SBOM per release (IEC 81001-5-1 5.5).
Add monthly evidence report: open critical/high CVEs vs SLA breaches.
Add runtime dependency monitoring (e.g., GitHub Dependabot + Snyk monitor for production digests).
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Continuous CI scan + monthly SBOM diff review + quarterly DC-SOUP-001 sign-off.

reviews.justification: Mandatory org_id filter at DB layer + API middleware enforcement + integration tests + periodic pen-testing constitute defence-in-depth aligned with UK GDPR Article 32 and the multi-tenant isolation pattern documented in NHS DTAC. Residual probability is improbable. Detectability rated 1 because integration tests run pre-deploy.
additional_controls_required: Annual third-party penetration test scoped explicitly to tenant-isolation (must include API and Cypher injection vectors).
Add property-based test that fuzzes Cypher queries to confirm org_id is non-optional.
Add runtime guard: log + alert any query executed without an org_id parameter.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Quarterly pen-test + continuous query-shape monitoring for missing org_id.

reviews.title_excerpt: Adversarial prompt injection via clinical text
reviews.justification: Comprehensive 8-control stack (INJECTION_GUARD, sanitise_for_prompt covering 15 pattern families, cap_llm_response, closed-set output validation, dual-model consensus, mode-aware fail-safe to UNCERTAIN, .cursor/rules/llm-security.mdc preventive control). Aligned with OWASP LLM Top-10 (LLM01 prompt injection, LLM02 insecure output handling). Probability of harm is improbable in autonomous mode due to fail-safe direction; novel injection patterns (GAP-017 unicode lookalikes) accepted as residual.
additional_controls_required: Quarterly red-team exercise with novel injection patterns to refresh sanitise_for_prompt rules.
Add unicode confusable normalisation (NFKC + confusable-detection) to close GAP-017.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Weekly review of prompt_safety logger, arbitrator_third_verdict warnings, and cap_llm_response truncation events for first 3 months post-launch.

reviews.title_excerpt: Privileged user creates malicious clinical rules
reviews.justification: Strong technical controls (admin-only routes, _validate_regex with ReDoS probe, literal length limits, server-side created_by from session). However the procedural admin-account control is rated 'partially_effective' and the periodic rule-audit + admin-action audit have empty implemented_by/verified_by arrays in the YAML, indicating no DI/VT linkage. Repudiation (R) and DoS (D) risks remain non-trivial because a single compromised admin can poison rules used by ALL future encounters before the monthly audit window. Conditionally acceptable until the rule-audit automation is implemented and proven.
additional_controls_required: Implement automated rule-impact pre-flight: any new context/suppress rule must show projected match-volume against last-30d encounter sample before activation.
Require 2-person approval (4-eyes) for ConText/post-processor rule creation; record approver in audit trail.
Add immutable append-only audit log for all admin actions (link to FMEA-054/R-131 control).
Add daily monitor: alert if any single context rule matches >= 5% of new encounters within 24h of activation.
Create a DI/VT for the procedural rule-audit so the monthly review has artefact backing.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Daily rule-impact monitor + monthly rule audit + quarterly admin access review with documented evidence.

reviews.title_excerpt: Clinical text exposed to multiple external LLM providers (DPA/DPIA gaps)
reviews.justification: UK/EEA data residency confirmed (AWS Bedrock eu-west-2 London; Azure OpenAI Sweden Central under UK Adequacy Regs 2021) - this materially reduces Article 44/46 transfer risk. However THREE open actions remain: (1) DPIA-001 (UK GDPR Article 35) not complete; (2) DPA-REVIEW-001 not complete (arbitration call to Sonnet not explicitly confirmed in DPA); (3) LOG-LLM-CALLS-001 per-call PHI audit log not implemented. Without per-call audit log, post-incident forensics for an Article 33 breach would be impaired (detectability rated 3). DPIA must be complete BEFORE production rollout to additional GP practices. Residual risk should NOT be downgraded to 'low' until all three actions close.
additional_controls_required: Complete DPIA-001 by 2026-06-01 (Article 35 mandatory for special-category processing).
Complete DPA-REVIEW-001 by 2026-05-01 with explicit confirmation of arbitration call coverage.
Complete LOG-LLM-CALLS-001 by 2026-05-15 with metadata-only logging (timestamp, provider, model_id, lengths, patient_id hash).
Add automated alert if Azure OpenAI region changes from Sweden Central.
Add RoPA entry for UK -> Sweden transfer with Article 45 adequacy basis cited.
Annual DPA review trigger; immediate review if provider ToS changes.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Monthly tracking of three open actions until closure; then quarterly DPA/region review. Block production rollout gate until DPIA-001 closed.

reviews.justification: Design-feature controls eliminate patient_id/encounter_id/org_id from learning-loop nodes; content-only SHA256 IDs; no graph relationships back to Patient/Encounter/Tenant; DI-ID gate blocks persistence on residual PHI patterns. Architectural data-protection-by-design satisfying UK GDPR Article 25. Residual risk is improbable because re-identification requires both content-hash collision AND ability to reconstruct the source corpus.
additional_controls_required: Quarterly automated field-audit (already in monitoring) should be wired into a CI test that fails on schema drift.
Add k-anonymity check on aggregated training exports if shared with research partners.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Quarterly automated KG schema scan + monthly DI-ID gate breach count (target = 0).

reviews.justification: User-level provenance moved out of KG nodes into AuditEvent in clinical graph. KG carries only system-level provenance. Aligned with data minimisation (Article 5(1)(c)) for shared/exported KG artefacts. Severity is minor because operator emails are work identifiers, not patient PHI. Quarterly KG PII field scan provides assurance.
additional_controls_required: Add CI lint that blocks new KG node properties matching email regex.
Document the AuditEvent retention policy (default 7y) in DSPT IG handbook.

reviews.title_excerpt: Unauthorised access to per-tenant AI costs/margin/discount
reviews.justification: Triple-layer access control (API 403 via _require_admin, AppShell adminOnly nav hiding, dashboard link gating). VT-LEO-AI-068 directly verifies 403 on three sensitive endpoints. No patient safety impact - business/commercial sensitivity only. Aligned with ISO 27001 A.5 access control.
additional_controls_required: Extend test coverage to all six /pricing/* endpoints (currently three explicitly verified).
Add IDOR test: authenticated tenant-A admin attempting GET /pricing/orgs/{tenant-B} must return 403.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Quarterly review of pricing_endpoint_403_rate; alert on sustained spike (probing).

reviews.title_excerpt: PHI leaks into NER training corpus via evidence_sentence
reviews.justification: Two independent PII checks (deidentify_with_span at storage; detect_phi() at export) plus monthly 500-record sweep + encounter/patient ID stripping. Architecture is sound and aligned with UK GDPR Article 25/35. Residual is critical-severity because any leak is an Article 33 notifiable breach with NLP-engineer access path. Conditional acceptability is correct: explicit conditions are DPIA completion, lawful-basis documentation, and a passing 500-record validation. Marking 'medium' (not 'low') until those conditions are evidenced; library limitations (deid.py is regex-only, see GAP-008) mean residual probability is unlikely not remote.
additional_controls_required: Complete DPIA for AI training corpus (separate lawful basis from direct care).
Document 500-record gold validation result and refresh quarterly.
Add NER-based PERSON detection layer to deid.py (close GAP-008).
Restrict training JSONL output location to encrypted-at-rest blob with named-engineer access list.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Monthly detect_phi() sweep; export_pii_gate_abort_count target 0; immediate incident response on any non-zero detection.

reviews.justification: Self-review detection is not implemented per CSV note ('Self-review detection not implemented' / 'Create R-LEO-AI-106'). Under NHS DCB0129 and IEC 62304 6.3, the same actor SHOULD NOT be able to create AND approve their own clinical rule, training label, or coding decision. Currently the system relies on procedural admin oversight (R-031). Without a technical conflict-of-interest (CoI) check, repudiation and elevation risks are real. Detectability rated 3 because CoI events would only surface in retrospective audit. R-LEO-AI-127 YAML must be created to formalise.
additional_controls_required: Implement server-side actor comparison: reject Approve when scope.email == record.created_by for training labels, coding decisions, and rule activations.
Override path with documented business reason + 2-person rule (4-eyes).
Add CoI metric to AuditEvent dashboard.
CREATE the missing risk YAML R-LEO-AI-127 per CSV CREATE_NEW action.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Daily CoI breach count (target 0 after enforcement); monthly review of override events with business-reason field.

reviews.justification: CSV note: 'Immutability not enforced at storage layer'. NHS DCB0129 clinical safety case AND UK GDPR Article 30 Records of Processing rely on a tamper-evident audit trail; without storage-layer immutability a privileged DBA or compromised service principal could rewrite history with no detectable trace. This is a foundational IG/security control gap and is currently UNACCEPTABLE for a SaMD Class B/C system processing special category data. Severity is critical because loss of audit integrity invalidates ALL downstream safety claims. R-LEO-AI-131 YAML must be created.
additional_controls_required: Implement append-only audit store: WORM blob (Azure immutable storage with legal-hold) OR cryptographically chained AuditEvent (hash-chain with periodic anchor publication).
Separate audit-write service principal from any admin/DBA role; remove DELETE/UPDATE permissions from audit collections.
Daily integrity verification job (recompute hash chain or check WORM seal).
CREATE risk YAML R-LEO-AI-131 with the above controls AND a VT covering tamper-attempt detection.
Block production rollout until at least the WORM storage option is in place.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Daily hash-chain integrity check; immediate paging alert on any failure; quarterly review of audit-store IAM.

reviews.title_excerpt: Audit trail entry missing for key decision (FMEA-055)
reviews.justification: CSV note: 'Event not emitted on all state change paths'. Audit completeness is a DCB0129 safety case prerequisite and an Article 5(2) accountability requirement. Today event emission is implemented opportunistically across routers/services - any missed path (e.g., bulk operations, re-tries, background corrections) creates a silent gap. Detectability rated 4 because missing events are by definition invisible in self-monitoring. R-LEO-AI-132 YAML must be created.
additional_controls_required: Inventory all state-changing operations on Patient, Encounter, CodingDecision, TrainingLabel, ContextRule, PostProcessorRule, AppropriatenessRule, AuditDomain, Tenant, User. Confirm every operation emits an AuditEvent.
Introduce a decorator/middleware pattern (@audited) so audit emission is declarative not opportunistic.
Add CI test: assert every router endpoint mutating a domain entity is annotated @audited or has an explicit waiver.
Reconciliation job: compare CodingDecision count delta vs AuditEvent count delta daily.
CREATE risk YAML R-LEO-AI-132 with above controls + VT.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Daily reconciliation between mutation count and audit-event count per entity type (drift threshold = 0).

reviews.justification: CSV note: 'Sandbox provisioning copies from production without de-identification'. This is a textbook UK GDPR Article 25 (data protection by design AND by default) violation and DSPT non-conformance: sandbox/test environments typically have weaker access controls, broader engineer access, and longer log retention. Even at 'unlikely' probability, real PHI in sandbox is unacceptable for SaMD on NHS data. Although CSV flags as 'safety_class A / Low probability', the IG impact is critical and merits Class B treatment. R-LEO-AI-154 YAML must be created.
additional_controls_required: Block production-to-sandbox copy at platform level; require synthetic data generator OR irreversible de-identification (k-anonymity + suppression) for any sandbox refresh.
Add Bicep/Terraform policy: deny role assignments that grant cross-environment subscription access.
Quarterly sandbox PHI scan with detect_phi() across all storage accounts.
Immediate purge procedure if PHI found in sandbox (with breach assessment trigger).
CREATE risk YAML R-LEO-AI-154; reclassify safety_class to B at minimum.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Quarterly sandbox PHI scan + monthly review of cross-environment IAM grants + automatic alert on any data-copy job touching production sources.

reviews.justification: CSV note: 'Exception not caught and sanitised before response'. Stack traces, DB error messages, file paths, and connection strings can leak via 5xx responses if FastAPI/router error handlers are inconsistent. While not patient PHI, this is an information-disclosure (STRIDE-I) risk that aids reconnaissance and may breach OWASP API Top-10 (API3:2023). NHS DSPT and ISO 27001 A.8.30 both expect sanitised error responses. R-LEO-AI-155 YAML must be created.
additional_controls_required: Global FastAPI exception handler returning {error_id, message='Internal error', timestamp}; full detail logged server-side only with the same error_id.
CI test: a faulting endpoint must NOT return any of: stack-trace markers, file-path patterns, password/token/key strings.
WAF/APIM rule to strip Server, X-Powered-By, and verbose error headers.
CREATE risk YAML R-LEO-AI-155.
reviews.monitoring_recommendation: Monthly review of 5xx response payload sample (target: 0 with internal detail); pen-test as part of annual security review.
